title: Auto-ISP: An Efficient Real-Time Automatic Hyperparameter Optimization Framework for ISP Hardware System
problem: ISP tuning is intricate and time-consuming, requiring substantial expertise. Current AI-based auto-tuning systems operate offline with predefined scenes and human intervention, failing to adapt to real-world unforeseen scenarios.
motivation: ISPs are widely deployed in edge devices and real-time automatic adaptation to varying conditions is essential for practical deployment without manual expertise.
method: The system uses a three-step optimization process built into custom hardware to automatically adjust image signal processor (ISP) settings in real-time as it processes camera feeds. Unlike traditional systems that require humans to pre-configure settings or need offline training on predefined scenes, this framework adapts on-the-fly to new situations. By designing the hardware and software together, it processes 1080P video at 75 frames per second on an FPGA (field-programmable chip) or 240 frames per second on an ASIC (application-specific integrated circuit).
key_novelty: Automatic real-time tuning of image signal processor settings that adapt to unforeseen camera scenes without requiring offline training on predefined examples.
contributions: Real-time automatic hyperparameter optimization framework for Image Signal Processors
Tri-step optimization framework that adapts to unforeseen scenes online
Hardware accelerator design for efficient ISP tuning on edge devices

metrics.accuracy: Superior performance in human and computer vision tasks
